children: CBOT grain futures are mixed with traders moving cautiously ahead of the U.S.-China summit. "Grain markets are basically in pause mode as traders await trade details from the meeting on Thursday between Xi Jinping and President Trump in Washington," says Brian Grete of Commstock Investments. Grete adds that the net long positions held by fund traders are another reason why traders are reluctant to push grains higher ahead of the summit--for fear of a large liquidation event if the meeting results in a negative sentiment. Most-active CBOT corn is down 0.6%, soybeans rise 0.1%, and wheat is off 0.6%. (kirk.maltais@wsj.com)
